newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Tobacco profits up despite harsh competition.
newsitem.headline: Japan Tobacco profits up despite harsh competition.

text.p: Japan Tobacco Inc, which dominates the country's gigantic tobacco market, announced higher half-year profits on Friday despite harsh competition from imported brands and a declining number of smokers.

Japan Tobacco said on Friday that its parent current profits increased 10.6 percent to 75.14 billion yen ($676 million) for the half-year that ended on September 30, against 67.93 billion yen ($611 million) in the year-ago period.
Current profit is pre-tax profit and includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.
The firm expects parent current profits for the full business year to nudge up 2.3 percent to 119 billion yen ($1.07 billion), against 116.35 billion yen ($1.04 billion) a year earlier.
Japan Tobacco was privatised in 1985, and it is still the only firm with the right to produce tobacco in Japan.
"The severe competition with foreign tobacco resulted in restricted sales, but higher prices on premium brands pushed up profits," a company spokesman said.
Analysts said the outlook of the tobacco industry was cloudy due to a falling number of smokers.
As a result, Japn Tobacco has expanded its business into a variety of new fields, from operating Burger King restaurants to developing biotechnology.
On Friday, the share price fell 5,000 yen ($45) to close at 802,000 yen ($7,225). ($1=111 yen)
